claim_samples.caveat: Institutional mandate, EOI, and handholding are not sustained private PSLV/SSLV output.
claim_samples.escalation: Obtain selected party, transfer agreement, realized vehicles, launch records, and annual production denominator.
claim_samples.subject: NSIL and IN-SPACe commercialization mechanisms
claim_samples.text: The commercialization pathway is institutionally real but should not be confused with proven high-rate private production. NSIL states that it is the commercial arm of ISRO, the nodal agency for PSLV production through an industry consortium, and an enabler of SSLV manufacturing through Indian industry. IN-SPACe has published an EOI for PSLV end-to-end technology transfer with ISRO handholding for 36 months or until two vehicles are realized and launched. These are enabling mechanisms. They do not, by themselves, establish private annual vehicle throughput. [15] [16] [17]

claim_samples.caveat: Machine or printer existence is not aerospace capability without controlled subcomponents, calibration, process monitoring, NDE, and qualification evidence.
claim_samples.escalation: Bind each product to approved machine, material/process, test asset, calibration, and acceptance records.
claim_samples.subject: Aerospace metrology and qualification chain
claim_samples.text: The strongest machine-builds-machine dependency is metrology and qualification. A 5-axis machining center is only an aerospace capability when its spindle, bearings, thermal stability, controller, servo performance, fixturing, tooling, calibration and process-monitoring chain are controlled. NIST notes that simultaneous five-axis geometric and servo errors compound and require standardized measurement/modeling. NASA’s AM work similarly shows that a printer is not the production system: powder/feedstock control, build parameters, support removal, heat treatment, HIP, final machining, NDE, dimensional inspection and component testing are all part of the lifecycle. [21] [22]

claim_samples.caveat: Factory announcements, installed machines, qualified processes, and repeated accepted deliveries are separate states and must not be merged.
claim_samples.escalation: Upgrade only with product-specific, dated, denominator-preserving qualification and accepted-delivery evidence.
claim_samples.subject: Unknown qualified capacity
claim_samples.text: For later FORGE simulations, the safest planning assumption is that **unknown qualified capacity is a hard constraint until evidence upgrades it**. A factory announcement may create a future-capacity node; a completed machine may create an installed-capacity node; a qualified process may create a usable-capacity node; and repeated accepted deliveries may create a demonstrated-throughput node. Those states should never be merged.
